findings.title: Mercy as protected communication
findings.claim: The exception-marked mercy and great favor in 17:87 portray revelation as a received, protected gift. The same exception phrase describes the unexpected reception of the Book at 28:86, and 4:113 pairs mercy and favor upon the Prophet with the Book, knowledge, and protection. The wider echoes connect this favor to communication and care; a bounded 4:1 root-family echo adds womb and kinship images of life-bearing care that extend toward human ties.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are raḥmatan, faḍlahu, kabīran, and rabbika, with the exception particle and ʿalayka supplying their local relations. The independent 28:86 trigger repeats illā raḥmatan min rabbika for the received Book; 4:113 joins mercy and favor to the Book, knowledge, and protection; 17:28 connects mercy from the Lord to gentle speech; 17:100 contrasts the Lord's mercy treasury with human withholding; 44:6 repeats mercy from your Lord with hearing and knowing; and 1:3 names divine mercy. These contacts make the favor a protective means of communication. Separately, 4:1's al-arhām in a shared-origin and kinship-duty setting activates a bounded womb/kinship analogy through the supplied root relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's greatness becomes a relation of gift, protection, and communicative access, while the 4:1 echo makes a distinct form of life-bearing and kinship care newly perceptible.
findings.containment: The 17:86 removal link is present only in the legacy walk summary; its Arabic surface is not embedded, so that part remains attributed. The 4:1 target morphology is also absent: the womb branch, kinship branch, and focus mercy remain distinct, and their contact is analogical. Connection 11:9 shows mercy withdrawn in another setting, 42:26 relates an added bounty to faithful response, and 67:9 shows warning can be denied. These limits bound this reading to the supplied contacts and leave recipient response and duration open.

epistemic.reason: Exact target Arabic at 28:86, 4:113, 17:28, 44:6, 1:3, 17:100, and 4:1 grounds the contextual contacts, and the cross-run focus support is trusted. The 17:86 removal relation comes only through a legacy walk; the 4:1 kinship/womb edge is analogical and its target morphology is not supplied.
